issues.body: `declares_sparq_gpu_dependency` still cannot support its claim of recognizing every Cargo spelling. TOML permits quoted keys, so `[dependencies]\n"sparq-gpu" = { path = "../sparq-gpu" }` and `[dependencies.alias]\n"package" = "sparq-gpu"` identify the same dependency but neither matches the textual checks. In addition, `nothing_in_the_workspace_depends_on_sparq_gpu` scans only the root manifest and immediate `crates/*/Cargo.toml` files rather than the actual workspace member set, so a member under another directory or a nested member is invisible. Thus a workspace dependency can still make the GPU code reachable while the deferral tripwire stays green.
issues.fix_hint: Use Cargo metadata or a TOML parser to enumerate the actual workspace member manifests and inspect dependency package identities, including renamed packages and quoted keys. Add regression fixtures for quoted dependency/package keys and for a workspace member outside the immediate `crates/*` layout; each should fail with the current implementation and pass after the fix.
issues.title: Dependency tripwire still does not cover Cargo's accepted manifest forms

verdict.summary: Round 2 remains blocked by the same major issue: the dependency detector is still a textual approximation while the documentation and test claim it catches every Cargo spelling. The ordinary renamed-dependency case from round 1 is now covered, but valid TOML quoted keys such as `"package" = "sparq-gpu"` or `"sparq-gpu" = { ... }` bypass the detector. The repository scan is also limited to direct children of `crates/`, so a workspace member elsewhere can depend on the crate without tripping it. Because the stated security-deferral trigger remains bypassable at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
